answer: Posted collateral must equal 8 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. Because the ember collateral is checked against the quill claim at intake, the harbor audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases as a result has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. That is 9 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
